questions.prompt: What is the relationship between a Charm and an Application in Juju?
options: A charm is the operational code package; an application is an instantiated deployment of that charm
A charm is a hardware host; an application is an operating system
A charm is a user account; an application is a security group
There is no difference; they are exact synonyms
questions.answer: A charm is the operational code package; an application is an instantiated deployment of that charm
questions.explanation: Charms contain the lifecycle logic from Charmhub. Deploying a charm into a model creates a running Application with one or more units.

questions.prompt: What does 'juju switch' do when given a controller and model name (e.g. 'pizzeria-controller:dev')?
options: It switches the active client context to target that specific controller and model for subsequent commands
It migrates all units from the first controller to the second
It destroys the active model and creates a new one
It changes the user password on the controller
questions.answer: It switches the active client context to target that specific controller and model for subsequent commands
questions.explanation: Context switching changes where all future CLI commands (like juju deploy or juju status) are executed.

questions.prompt: Where does the Juju state database reside?
options: On the local client machine in ~/.local/share/juju
Directly inside each deployed charm unit
questions.explanation: The Juju controller runs MongoDB to maintain the entire state of models, machines, applications, and relations.
